_note: Copy to docs/work/checklist/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<subject>.json. Never fill this file in place. status is pass|fail|skipped|substituted; substituted means checked by a different instrument than the item names, and its reason must say which. accepted stays null until a human answers it, so an unfinished run is visibly unfinished. Delete any item whose feature no longer exists rather than skipping it.

run.commit: 53ec9f20 (tree for derived facts); installed binary 1.57.6+79b79407 from nuget.org
run.data-root: per lane under the session scratchpad (lane-a/b/c); ~/.ai-raccoon read only (lane B copied memory.db), port 7721 never bound
run.note: Full run, three parallel lanes. Verifies the PUBLISHED 1.57.6 package (no local build); adds pooled-open-concurrency-smoke for ADR-0131.

findings-against-prior-runs.finding: None contradicted. Re-derived: the 1.57.2 run's port-7721 'unchanged pid' check relied on a live owner server; in this run no server listened on 7721 at all, so the same wording cannot be reused blindly - the check degrades to 'nothing bound 7721'.

Environment note, not a prior-run error: three stdio proxy processes (pids 69134, 81074, 1140, started Oct 12-13) still execute the deleted pre-update 1.57.5 binary from ~/.dotnet/tools/.store/.stage/lr4nerht.5qo; any evidence gathered through those proxies (e.g. the connected ai-raccoon MCP tools in an agent session) reflects 1.57.5, not the installed 1.57.6. This lane used its own 1.57.6 server throughout.

Driver needs `X-AiRaccoon-Token` from <data-root>/mcp-token for /mcp; the memory/prior notes do not mention this, and the prior drivers (/tmp/air1572/*) no longer exist - a reusable driver in the repo would save every run rewriting it.
memory-write: also run 1.57.2 hash identity: hash b4faa710... is identical to the 1.57.2 run's astro hash, so it is content/context-stable, not a per-run value.

keyword-search-across-a-chunk-boundary: the checklist's literal fixture (sentence x10 + vk83jq) no longer produces more than one entries row on this build (1 row, len 1189) because the memory chunk window is 1022 tokens (ADR-0125); the item's own premise ('more than one entries row') cannot hold for it. The 1.57.2 run noticed (x45 fallback) but the template text was not updated. Template should specify a note long enough (>~4,700 chars) or a size sweep; a sweep of 90 sizes here placed the id within 14 chars of the cut and never split it.

read-path-query-guard: the 1.57.2 structural-detector step used a 30-line stack-frame query; that shape trips the regex warn tier (StackFrameLineRegex) on its own, so the 'warns when armed' leg could not distinguish the structural detector. This run used a log-line shape with no regex marker; only then does the 'off vs on' difference prove the detector. The previous verdict was right about the outcome but the instrument could not fail.

long-query-keyword-terms-capped: 1.57.2 recorded 1.70 s for the 7,259-char paste at vw0; 1.57.6 measured 7-10 s on a fresh 23,243-entry copy. Cause here is host load (load average 43-47, another lane's server at ~745% CPU), confirmed by the 1.56.0 control being 4-40x slower under the same load, not a regression. Timings need an idle host to be comparable across runs.

sqlite3 -readonly ~/.ai-raccoon/memory.db fails with 'unable to open database file' when the live server is not holding the WAL (no -shm); SKILL.md already mentions this for scratch banks, but the checklist's VACUUM INTO route for the live bank is the same trap. Copying the file (cp) works when no -wal file exists.

search results collapse identical-text rows from different notes into one result (82 distinct texts of 91 rows holding the id); an expectation of 'every row holding the id is returned' must compare distinct values, not rows.

1.57.2 promotion-queue-state: it concluded 'memory_share_extract propose added no additional candidates ... a property of the small fixture'. The real cause: SelectExtractionCandidates (MemorySql.cs:54-63) only admits rows with embed_state='embedded', and that fixture had no embedding engine so every row was pending. With an engine configured, propose returns ranked candidates immediately. The prior run only ever exercised the agent-requested-share path (a fixed score 5) and never the scorer.

1.57.2 watch-catch-up premise note: its driver used chmod 000 on node_modules so the node_modules decoy could never be read; that decoy proves nothing about exclusion (a hidden-dir decoy, or an unlocked node_modules, is the real control).

docs/reference/logging-event-ids.md is missing event ids emitted at runtime in these runs: 703 (PromotionQueueService, Discarded N queued row(s)), 1003 (embed drain pass finished) and 1005 (embed drain pass failed) are in src (PromotionQueueService.cs:304, EmbedDrainReporter.cs:85,93) but grep of the reference finds no row for them: the Observability item's 'ids resolve against the reference' check would fail for these. Not tracked by this lane; report to the observability lane/owner.
docs/reference/agent-memory-server.md writes watch states lowercase (healthy) while memory_watch_status returns 'Healthy' (PascalCase).

CORRECTION to lane C's finding that events 703, 1003, 1005 lack a row in docs/reference/logging-event-ids.md: they are covered by ranged rows '700, 702-704, 707-709' (line 214) and '1002-1013' (line 231). Lanes A and B resolved them correctly. Not a doc gap.

CORRECTION to lane B's 'stale premise' finding on keyword-search-across-a-chunk-boundary: the template was already updated. It specifies the sentence forty-five times ('ten fit in one chunk since 1.56'). Lane B took the 10x fixture from the 2026-10-05 1.57.2 run file, not the template. Its size-sweep substitute still exercised the premise (54 multi-row notes), so the item verdict stands, and the template needs no change.

items.expected-result: ADR-0121: while the server is stopped, x.md (same size, mtime between its watch_files.updated_at and watches.last_change_ts) and w.md (different size, mtime older than its own updated_at) are re-digested on restart, judged by each file's own fingerprint: watch_files.file_hash changes to SHA-256(path+content) of the new bytes, updated_at/size update; new terms searchable, old terms gone; decoy terms in .git-like and node_modules dirs never found; y.md (unchanged) keeps its hash.
items.command: watch wd/c with x.md,w.md,y.md + node_modules/pkg/index.md (chmod 000) + hidden decoy dir; wait 3 watch_files rows; edit y.md so last_change_ts moves; sqlite3 -readonly while serving; kill server; rewrite x.md same size and os.utime 1791894209; rewrite w.md 21->25 bytes and os.utime 1791894207; restart same data root (60878); sleep 12; sqlite3 watch_files; memory_search each term (FTS5-only, no engine configured); independent python sha256(path+content)
items.evidence: premise (server up, before stop): x.md updated_at=1791894208 size 21, last_change_ts=1791894211; x.md edited mtime=1791894209 -> 208 <= 209 <= 211 holds; w.md mtime 1791894207 < its updated_at 1791894208, size 21 -> 25. pre: x.md hash 8af50b0b... updated 208; w.md cb98e1d1... updated 208. post-restart: x.md 0c29a366... updated 1791894236 size 21; w.md abe2c2dd... updated 1791894236 size 25; y.md hash cb8df74d... unchanged (updated_at 236 = hash-skip touch). Independent sha256(path+bytes): x 0c29a36659a1ade8..., w abe2c2dd612b9438... match the bank. memory_search: xylophonebbb -> hit x.md; walrusnewterm777 -> hit w.md; xylophoneaaa, walrusold111, nmzzzterm, gitzzzterm -> results [] ; yakyakyak -> hit y.md.
items.observed-result: Both missed changes were healed on restart, from the file's own fingerprint: x.md was missed by the old 'mtime > last_change_ts' rule (its mtime was < last_change_ts) yet re-digested; w.md healed via size change despite an mtime older than its fingerprint. Bank hash equals independently computed hash of the on-disk bytes for both. Old terms purged, decoy terms never indexed. Caveat: the node_modules decoy is confounded by chmod 000 (unreadable regardless); the hidden-directory decoy is the unconfounded exclusion control. The 5-minute heal pass (event 322, Debug) was not exercised.
items.acceptance-reason: Judged against the file's own stored hash and stamp, with the premise window verified before the restart. 5-minute timer path is optional per the item and was not run.

Unknown embedding provider') because the fresh scratch root has no embedding engine configured - expected on an unconfigured bank, and the same id appeared in the 1.57.2 run.

items.expected-result: under heavy concurrent bank-opening MCP calls spanning more than one pool-prune interval (2-4 min), zero failed calls and zero ObjectDisposedException / SQLitePCL.sqlite3 lines in the server log (ADR-0131)
items.command: tools/stress.py 65262 420 64: 64 threads each with its own MCP session looping memory_search/memory_list/memory_stats/memory_write/memory_get(unknown hash) for 420 s, plus a file watch on a dir whose files are edited every 5 s; then grep -c -E 'ObjectDisposed|SQLitePCL|cannot start a transaction|Watch re-watch reconcile pass failed' over lc1.log+lc2.log
items.observed-result: 112,155 calls across 64 concurrent sessions over 421 s (more than one full 2-4 min prune interval, so at least one prune ran) completed with zero failed calls and zero race signatures in the log. memory_get with a 64-zero hash is expected to refuse and was asserted to refuse. The watch reconcile path produced no log lines either way, so I cannot show it actually ran in the window.
items.acceptance-reason: Accept as pass-with-caveat only. The race (dotnet/efcore#39008) is nondeterministic and I did not run the same load against 1.57.5 to see it reproduce, so absence here is weak evidence: this run could not have distinguished a fixed build from a lucky run. It does show the serialized-open gate causes no deadlock/failures under 64-way contention; the real proof of the fix is the unit/integration tests in ADR-0131's PR.
